sections.h2: How do I reach the Register of Deeds in Marion, McDowell County?
sections.html:
Go to 35 West Fort Street, or phone 828-652-4727. The county posts weekday hours of 8:30am to 5:00pm, and it sends people to McDowellDeeds.com for services online.

The county describes the office's work as recording, indexing and storing real estate and business documents. The same counter handles marriage licenses, notary oaths and commissions, veterans' discharge records, and certified copies of recorded documents plus birth and death records. For a seller, the real estate side is the one that matters, and the registrar's stated aim is a record that is complete, accurate and kept safe.

sections.h2: Does McDowell County accept electronic recording?
sections.html:
It does, for every kind of document, per the county's own statement. Three vendors are listed, so an attorney in another city can file without a trip to Marion.

Vendors named by McDowell County for electronic filing
VendorTelephone
Simplifile1-800-460-5657
Electronic Document Logistics (EDL)1-919-341-4101
Corporation Service Company (CSC)1-866-652-0111

Your attorney or title company picks among them, so you will seldom call any yourself. Your job is getting the signed deed ready.

sections.h2: What fees apply to a McDowell County deed filing?
sections.html:
McDowell County applies the statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10, with no local add-ons. Expect these items.

  • A deed or ordinary instrument: $26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 for each further page.
  • A deed of trust or mortgage: $64.00 through page 35, then $4.00 per further page.
  • A lender's release of a deed of trust: nothing.
  • A plat: $21.00 a sheet.
  • Certified copies: $5.00 for page one and $2.00 for the rest.
  • A nonstandard format: $25.00 extra. A second instrument inside one document: $10.00 extra.

The statute calls the schedule complete and exclusive and has the fee paid before filing. For a 60-page bundle of exhibits, phone 828-652-4727 and ask the office to total it.

sections.h2: Who owes the transfer tax on a McDowell County sale?
sections.html:
Sellers carry this one. G.S. 105-228.30 sets $1.00 for every $500 of price, with any remainder under $500 counted as a full unit, and the registrar takes payment first.

Half stays with the county. Of the other half, the state receives monthly remittances after refunds and the county's allowance.

Your closing statement prints the amount in the seller column, beside the loan payoff and any tax owed.

sections.h2: What happens to a deed after it is recorded in McDowell County?
sections.html:
The county's assessor page says the GIS mapping department processes deed transfers and updates the county maps. The same department acts as plat review officer. That puts deed transfers and parcel maps in the same hands, so check the map after your deed is recorded.

The assessor's office is at 60 E. Court Street, with the same weekday hours, and the page lists extensions for real property, mapping and land records. It also announces a 2027 real property reappraisal, which matters to a seller because a reappraisal changes the value a buyer will inherit.

  • Ask land records or mapping whether your parcel is mapped as you expect.
  • Ask the real property staff how a reappraisal could affect the assessment.
  • Report storm damage through the link on the assessor's page.

The tax collector at (828) 652-0701 can give you a payoff figure for the current bill.

sections.h2: Which McDowell County tax relief programs follow a house into a sale?
sections.html:
Check the parcel for a relief program before you sign a contract, because some of them change at transfer. McDowell County's assessing office takes applications from January 1 through May 31 at 60 East Court Street, with everything due back by June 1, and an applicant may use only one program.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: $25,000 or half of assessed value off the home and up to an acre, whichever is greater, with no lien. It requires age 65 by January 1 or total disability, and the county says to call for the yearly income figure.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of assessed value, one application, no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: five prior years of ownership and occupancy plus a yearly June 1 application. The latest three years of deferred tax are a lien until paid, and a death, a transfer or a move out triggers payment.
  • Present-use value: for farm, forest and horticulture land, applied for in January, with a sound management plan for forest land.

If the parcel is in present-use value or has deferred circuit breaker tax, tell your closing attorney so the back amounts are priced into the settlement.

sections.h2: How do McDowell County tax foreclosure auctions work?
sections.html:
Judicial tax foreclosures follow G.S. 105-374, and the county holds the auctions at the courthouse, 21 S. Main St. in Marion. At the close of the sale, the top bidder leaves $1,000.00 in cash with the commissioner.

After that comes a 10-day window for upset bids, which are handled in the clerk's office. Each one has to top the previous bid by 5 percent, and by at least $750.00. A new bid restarts the 10 days. The county lists the clerk at (828) 655-4100.

  • Pending sales are listed on a link from the county's foreclosure page.
  • Map, assessed value, acreage and deed reference come from the GIS, searched by parcel number.
  • Wells and septic questions are left to the bidder to research, perhaps through a neighbor.

An owner behind on tax who sells first avoids all of this. Call the tax collector for the payoff before an auction date is set.

sections.h2: Why does the order of recording matter for a McDowell County house?
sections.html:
First to register wins priority. G.S. 47-18 withholds a deed's force against lien creditors and paying purchasers until it is filed where the land is located, which for a McDowell parcel means the Marion counter.

Attorneys therefore file the deed and the buyer's loan documents together. They also make sure old releases are filed, since cancellations cost nothing but depend on how fast a lender responds. If your title search finds a lien that was never cancelled, ask the attorney to chase the release early.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about selling in McDowell County?
sections.html:
Census figures show 45,198 residents in mid-2025 versus 44,578 counted in 2020. There were 22,036 housing units in 2025 and 18,638 households across 2020 to 2024, 75.6 percent of homes being owner-occupied.

Owner-occupied homes carried a median value of $171,100, median gross rent was $806, and median household income was $57,168 in 2024 dollars. The county issued 164 building permits in 2025. About 2,760 veterans live in the county, and a disabled veteran may qualify for the $45,000 exclusion under G.S. 105-277.1C.

Land covers 439.95 square miles, close to 101 people per square mile. Inherited houses, probate sales and homes needing work are frequent reasons owners look at cash offers here, and a buyer paying cash can close once the deed is ready to record.

faqs.q: When can I visit the McDowell County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm, at 35 West Fort Street, Marion. Call 828-652-4727.

faqs.q: Which vendors file McDowell County deeds electronically?
faqs.a: Simplifile, EDL (Electronic Document Logistics) and CSC (Corporation Service Company). The county says any document can go this way.

faqs.q: What does McDowell County charge for a 12-page deed?
faqs.a: $26.00, since the base fee covers up to 15 pages. A deed of trust has its own $64.00 base for up to 35 pages.

faqs.q: Which party pays McDowell County's deed excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller, at $1.00 per $500 of price, paid at the counter ahead of filing.

faqs.q: How much must an upset bid add at a McDowell County tax sale?
faqs.a: At least 5 percent over the last bid, and never under $750.00 more. It goes through the clerk's office, and each bid resets a 10-day period.
